title: Ops dashboard interaction & trace-linking lab notes
body:
Purpose:
Quick field notes capturing a small experiment plan and naming conventions for linking visual widgets to trace artifacts. Target audience: operations, SREs, and product owners working on the console's incident workflow. This is NOT a final spec — it’s a lab notebook for iterations.

Summary / motivation:
We keep seeing long investigation time when tokenized requests spike: dashboards point at an anomaly but the operator has to run several ad-hoc queries to map that tile to the exact trace that shows KV-cache eviction or cross-region routing. Goal: reduce mean time to root cause by making the dashboard–>trace path a 1-click (or 1-hover) interaction, with consistent metric names and ownership annotations so responders can quickly route to a team.

Scope and constraints:
- UX changes restricted to operator-facing microinteractions (no full redesign).
- Back-end must support lightweight trace lookup endpoints (by session-id, request-path-hash, tenant, model, prefix-key).
- Must be cost-conscious: avoid forcing full-trace expansion for every tile refresh; rely on sampling + fast indexed pointers.
- Privacy: strip PHI before trace preview, maintain existing redaction rules.

Proposed metric & trace naming conventions (short, machine-friendly):
- metric.name: runtime.latency.token_first_ms (histogram: ms quartiles, p50/p90/p99 buckets)
- metric.name: runtime.kvcache.hit_rate (gauge: 0-1, per-tenant sampling)
- metric.name: routing.fanout.multimodel (count per request)
- metric.name: request.retries.count (counter)
- trace.tag keys: t.tenant, t.model, t.commit, t.route_policy, t.kvcache_state
- trace.span.name convention: serve.<stage> e.g., serve.kv_lookup, serve.attention_forward, serve.kv_evict
- widget.annotation key: owner:team-slug (e.g., owner:eng-serving-runtime)
Why this set: narrow, predictable names reduce aliasing when dashboards create quick links. The trace.tag prefix 't.' helps search tooling avoid collisions.

Trace-to-widget linking patterns (UX primitives):
1) hover-preview (cheap): hover on a chart point -> small modal with top-3 sampled traces summary (duration, top-level span names, owner tag, short hash). No full trace expansion.
2) quick-open (medium): click -> open right-side panel with full trace viewer but pre-filtered to spans that contributed to the chosen latency bucket (highlights).
3) deep-dive (heavy): click "open raw" -> full trace in new tab with full timing and logs. This action will be rate-limited to avoid load.

Back-end index surface needed:
- index by (tenant, model, minute-bucket, route_policy) -> list of trace pointers (trace_id, root_duration_ms, top_spans, owner). Keep rolling TTL 24h/7d depending on retention tier.
- quick-lookup endpoint: GET /api/trace-pointer?tenant=...&model=...&time=...&heat_bucket=... returns top-N pointers (N=10).
- preview endpoint: POST /api/trace-preview with pointer list -> returns sanitized summary for hover cards.

Sampling & cost rules:
- Always keep deterministic sampling for errors (capture 100% of ERROR traces for 24h).
- Latency tail sampling: capture 100% above p99.9 for model-serving spans for short-term retention window.
- Otherwise, reservoir sampling at 0.5% per tenant by default; priority tenants (enterprise) get 2%.

Dashboard interaction patterns (implementation notes):
- Widgets must emit the exact metric.name used in backend; dashboards should include the widget.annotation.owner field as metadata so operator can route immediately.
- When a widget shows an alert, attach a generated timeline card with the top 3 trace pointers in the same minute window. This timeline is cached for 60s.
- For stacked area charts (token latency breakdown), clicking on a slice should populate the quick-open with span-level highlights (ex: KV lookup latency slice -> highlight serve.kv_lookup spans across sampled traces).

Ownership & routing conventions:
- Widget annotations: owner:team-slug, oncall:email (optional). Owner is REQUIRED for any operational tile that feeds an alert.
- If no owner, UI shows a small "assign" CTA that creates a lightweight ownership ticket (jira:ENGOBS-XXXX) with the widget metadata.
- Team-routing rules: when operator hits "escalate" from preview, system should copy a minimal context snippet (metric snapshot + trace pointer + a short prompt) to the team’s incident channel (Slack/X).

Example operator workflow (happy path):
1) Dashboard shows p99 spike for runtime.latency.token_first_ms in us-west-2.
2) Hover preview shows two trace pointers with owner:eng-serve and owner:eng-routing.
3) Click quick-open on pointer 1 -> right panel opens, highlights serve.kv_evict spans at 120ms. The operator tags "eng-serve" and attaches the trace pointer to the incident.

Edge cases & privacy:
- Airgapped/private deployments: preview endpoint must only return metadata; do not attempt remote lookups outside VPC.
- When trace sampling is low for a tenant, show a clear badge: "low coverage: request sampling 0.5% — increase for deeper thread."

Experiments we want to run (A/B):
- A: hover-preview shows top-3 vs B: top-1 only, measure time-to-escalate and click-through rate over 2 weeks.
- A: highlight spans by absolute time vs B: highlight by proportion-of-request (which is more intuitive for requests with many tokens).
- Track metric: mean time from alert to team assignment (goal < 6 minutes).

Open questions / decisions to make:
- TTL for trace-pointer index for non-enterprise tenants: 24h vs 72h? Cost trade-offs documented in ENGOBS-512.
- How to represent retries: aggregate into single pointer vs show separate pointers per retry attempt.
- Which UI library for right-panel trace viewer to avoid reimplementing (options: reuse internal trace UI vs embed open-source viewer).

TODO (near-term action items):
- [ ] Engineer: prototype /api/trace-pointer and /api/trace-preview (Harpreet) — estimate: 2w.
- [ ] UX: low-fidelity hover card and right-panel mockups (Liam) — estimate: 4 days.
- [ ] SRE: define sampling knobs and default % per tenant class (Diego) — 1 week.
- [ ] Product: define ownership badge schema and escalation CTA wording (Maya) — this doc finalization then PR.

Notes to self / informal observations:
- Operators often want an immediate readout: not a full flame-graph. Keep preview terse.
- Naming collisions are a real source of friction; prefer short consistent prefixes (runtime., request., routing.).
- We should add a short education card in the dashboard intro about what each owner tag means and where to escalate.

Appendix (quick glossary):
- trace pointer: compact index entry (trace_id + summary) used for fast lookup.
- heat_bucket: small integer representing p50/p90/p99/p999 buckets used for quick filtering.
- widget annotation: small JSON blob attached to a widget describing owner, alert severity, metric.name.

If you review this, please add comments inline in the Google doc and drop a +1 on the UX mock PR when available.

-- Maya
